references.text: Complementary journeys: The descent to Egypt (Gen 46:6) and the ascent from Egypt (Gen 45:25) mark the beginning and end of the Egyptian exile period for Jacob's descendants.

Thematic parallel: Jacob's journey from Paddan-Aram with his entire household foreshadows and mirrors later patriarchal movements, but here there is a contrast in direction (to Canaan versus to Egypt).
Typological parallel: Abraham's arrival in Canaan with his entire household (Gen 12:5) is a precursor to Jacob's arrival in Egypt with the same description of gathering possessions.
Contrast: While Esau leaves Canaan with his possessions to flee from Jacob (Gen 36:6), Jacob is brought to Egypt with his possessions as part of God's redemptive history.
Direct narrative connection: Gen 1:1 confirms and summarizes the event in Gen 46:6 by listing the names of those who came to Egypt with Jacob.
Theological contrast: Abraham's ascent from Egypt (Gen 13:1) mirrors and contrasts Jacob's descent to Egypt (Gen 46:6), marking cycles of exile and deliverance.
Allusion and summary: 1 Sam 12:8 explicitly refers to the event in Gen 46:6 as the starting point for Israel's time in Egypt before the Exodus.
